## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Need to migrate `unique_id` from `<name>_<type_of_sensor>` to `<ble_address>_<type_of_sensor>`. This will make everything easier, including maintaining this integration. Unfortunately I introduced a bug in [this PR](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/97905), which caused new entities to be changed.

This PR will try to migrate the entities from pre 2023.9 release. If not found the entities introduced in 2023.9.0 will be migrated. And if it finds the _newest_ and correct unique id, it will just skip the migration.

Also adding identifiers to the device, which was completely missing.

Should probably have made some tests for this, but I'm not 100% sure how to test the migration.

Refactored the code a bit. Moved the `unique_id` migration from `__init__.py` to `sensor.py` so I could drop the regex to find the sensor type (end of the `unique_id`). This also makes the loop much easier to read, less "magic" (regex) and it migrates one sensor type at the time (e.g. temperature) instead of going through every sensor.

issue_context.title: Airthings BLE does not meet unique id requirements; All entities recreated in 2023.9.x+
issue_context.body:
### The problem

#97905 Was indeed a breaking change, it left my long term radon sensors forever unavailable, and then created duplicate entities with a different name, with no long term history tied to it.
There was no migration.
I'm tracking radon levels, and it's very important to have the long term history on that. HA v2023.9 broke that.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.9

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2023.8

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Airthings BLE

It should have kept its entity id based on unique ID. But.. https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/0c7e0f5cd92f68b7ef772e11f832f68392a2fe46/homeassistant/components/airthings_ble/sensor.py#L168 is bad. The name of a device is part of the unique id. This must be corrected. 

@LaStrada think you can look at correcting this unique id? Also perhaps adding yourself as maintainer.
@sdrapha i think you should be able to remove the old entity, and rename the entity id of the new entities to the old name to retain history. But agree it should not have been breaking.

@elupus thanks for the reply, I'll create a cloned container to test that, if that doesn't work, I'll try to use sudo to mess around with `core.entity_registry` inside the `.storage` folder. Trying to merge back the entities.

So, if I understood correct, the unique_id is created from the name, therefore, since last PR changed the names, it consequentially also changed the unique_ids, hence, entirely new entities... that is why it didn't linked to the previously existing ones.

> #97905 Was indeed a breaking change

Its not an intentional breaking change, its a bug. Unfortunately the unique ids have been using the name since the initial merge in #77284 so they never met the [unique id requirements](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/entity_registry_index?_highlight=unique&_highlight=id&_highlight=re#unique-id-requirements) 😢

I didn't notice the problem was already there in the existing code when I reviewed #97905 

The unique ids likely need to be migrated to use the `address` instead of the `name`

We could revert https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/97905 that should at least prevent anyone else who hasn't upgraded from hitting the issue until someone can find the time to migrate the entities to use a proper unique id
Not sure if thats better or worse because that means anyone who fixed it manually would have to do it again and it would make it harder to reconcile the history.

> @sdrapha i think you should be able to remove the old entity, and rename the entity id of the new entities to the old name to retain history. But agree it should not have been breaking.

I've just tried that manual fix, it didn't completely work, deleting the old entities, and renaming the newer ones with the old name, that will fix automations and frontend cards, but the recorded states from the old entities didn't show up, only the newly recorded states. So I think it's all tied up to the `unique_ids` in the end, it doesn't matter the `entity_id` being the correct one.

If you did it manually by moving things around in the registry it won't make the api calls to move around the history data.

It should still all be in there if you want to manually relink it via the `states_meta` table

Be sure to make a backup first

I did it through the UI, entity settings dialogue.
I'm doing all that manual fixing in a cloned container I made, so if I break stuff, I can just nuke it, and go back to the original.

So, taking a look at `core.entity_registry`, on the image bellow, side by side, one is the old entity, and the other is the new entity, the only difference on the `unique_id`'s is the parenthesis.

![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/25059996/2f4194fd-f970-4b6e-9687-ee18bcee1f70)

I'm not familiar with `states_meta` but I'll research and learn. I'm guessing you are talking about accessing the sql database directly to fix it...but I'll find out.

For whoever is interested in my saga of manually relinking the entities: 
I successfully manually relinked them, by renaming the `unique_id` of the OLD entities, to include the parenthesis from the new code, and then deleted the NEW entities entirely, all on `core.entity_registry`, it's all working fine now, I've got a gap on the history, but a minor one, I still have the long term values on the correct working entities now.

When a REAL fix for the issue is released, I can relink the entities again manually if necessary.
I doubt many people, or any at all, will follow my manual fix path, so a real fix for the `unique_id` standards would be ideal.

review_comments: Please use f-strings instead of string concatenation.

I'd store the expected unique id in a local variable so we don't rely on the details of the entity registry implementation creating new entity registry entry instances on update. If that would not happen, this check would be useless as it would compare the same attribute on the same instance.
